settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_URL
settings.description: The shared Redis, as redis://[user[:password]@]host[:port][/db] or rediss:// for TLS; unset keeps each store in one node's memory

when_wrong.detail: A URL that does not parse, a scheme other than redis or rediss, or redis:// under the production profile: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests, and the log says why without the password. From 0.6.0 a redis:// URL under the production profile also refuses the components that use Redis at start-up

settings.name: REDIS_URL
settings.description: The shared Redis when OIDF_REDIS_URL and its property are unset: the name Railway and most managed Redis providers export; read as OIDF_REDIS_URL is

when_wrong.detail: As OIDF_REDIS_URL, when it is read: while OIDF_REDIS_URL or oidf.redis.url is set, REDIS_URL is not read and the production profile does not judge it

settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_CA_FILE
settings.description: A PEM file of the CA certificates to trust for rediss://, in place of the JVM's; the server's certificate must still name the host

when_wrong.detail: A file that cannot be read or holds no certificate: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests, naming the file

settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_POOL_SIZE
settings.description: The most connections the client holds open at once, in use or idle

when_wrong.detail: Not a whole number from 1 to 256

settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_BORROW_TIMEOUT_MS
settings.description: How long a command waits for a connection when all of them are in use, before it fails as Redis unavailable

when_wrong.detail: Not a whole number from 1 to 60000

settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS
settings.description: How long one command may take once it has a connection: connecting, the TLS handshake, AUTH, finding the master and the one retry included

when_wrong.detail: Not a whole number from 1 to 60000

settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_SENTINEL_MASTER
settings.description: The master's name in Redis Sentinel; set with OIDF_REDIS_SENTINELS, the client asks the sentinels where the master is instead of dialling the URL's host

when_wrong.detail: Set without OIDF_REDIS_SENTINELS, or the other way round: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests; a name the sentinels do not know makes every command fail as Redis unavailable

settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_SENTINELS
settings.description: The sentinels, as host:port separated by spaces or commas (port 26379 when left out), asked in order; TLS and the CA file apply to them as to the master

when_wrong.detail: An entry that is not host or host:port: every store that would use Redis refuses its requests, naming the entry

settings.name: OIDF_REDIS_SENTINEL_PASSWORD
settings.description: The password the sentinels ask for, when they ask for one (the master's comes from the URL)

when_wrong.detail: The sentinels refuse AUTH and every command fails as Redis unavailable
